transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (Borealis HoS), Liam O'Connor (Procurement), Sofia Martinez (Cloud Architect)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood walked through SIG/CAIQ mapping and which evidence is typically provided by Redwood vs customer. Discussion about KMS key management responsibilities for private vs hosted, audit log retention, and the mechanics for delivering evidence (secure upload vs portal). Action items: Redwood to send cert/evidence links; Borealis to assign SIG owners and confirm residency.

Topics: SIG strategy, evidence handoff model, KMS and encryption, VPC/private deployment, audit logs retention and exports, SOC 2 & ISO artifacts

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you blocking the time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Anita Rao: Anita here. thanks.
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Liam on procurement, good to meet you all.
[00:09] Sofia Martinez: Sofia here, cloud arch.
[00:12] Devon Park: Devon from Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Cool, the plan for today is to go through our typical SIG/CAIQ approach and then talk through evidence handoff — you know the practical bits like who owns the KMS keys, where artifacts live, and what we can pre-fill. any priorities we should hit first?
[00:30] Anita Rao: Uh yes — data residency is big for us, plus we need clarity on where logs land and whether Redwood can provide unredacted audit trails for review. also SOC 2 evidence timeline.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. we'll flag data residency first. Devon, do you want to start with the CAIQ mapping?
[00:44] Devon Park: Sure. so, in our view the SIG/CAIQ is mostly a mapping exercise: some questions are "provider responsibility" and some are "customer responsibility." for example encryption at rest — Redwood provides the managed encryption for hosted models; that includes KMS-backed keys in our control for hosted tenants, we can provide key rotation records and attestation. for private deployments, customers typically bring their own KMS and manage keys — that's when we mark it as customer responsibility.
[01:18] Sofia Martinez: when you say "hosted" do you mean the Redwood shared cloud offering or Redwood Dedicated? because we have a hybrid constraint — some workloads must be in our VPC.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Good call — hosted means our public managed API. Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity which can be delivered in a customer VPC or dedicated tenancy depending on the contract. Devon?
[01:36] Devon Park: Right — for Dedicated in a VPC we support customer-managed KMS (bring your own key) and HSM integrations on request. there can be nuances: e.g., audit logs — by default for hosted we surface summarized logs in the console and provide export endpoints; for Dedicated/VPC we can ship raw, per-request audit logs to a customer-owned storage endpoint.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: Okay, and what about retention? our policy requires 7 years for certain financial traces. is that doable?
[02:12] Devon Park: Seven years is long. We can retain exports for the duration of the contract for Dedicated deployments if we configure long-term bucket retention on the customer's storage. for hosted customers we keep detailed telemetry for 90 days by default and aggregated metrics longer — long retention is an enterprise add-on and often involves offloading logs to your storage.
[02:36] Anita Rao: Are those export endpoints push or pull? we need SFTP or a secure push into an internal bucket.
[02:43] Devon Park: Typically it's a push to an S3-compatible endpoint with TLS and signed credentials; we can also set up an SFTP transfer to an intermediary if that's required. we'll document the exact mechanism in the evidence plan.
[02:55] Maya Chen: Let's talk SOC 2 and ISO artifacts. Devon — what do you usually provide for SOC 2?
[03:01] Devon Park: We provide the SOC 2 Type II report summary, description of controls, and selected evidence like change control logs, incident response runbooks, and the attestation PDF from the auditor. we can share a redacted version of some logs when necessary. full raw logs are typically only available in Dedicated/VPC scenarios.
[03:21] Anita Rao: Redacted versions are okay for now, but we may request raw logs for a deep audit later. what's the path for that?
[03:28] Devon Park: That would be an escalation and usually involves a compliance engagement with our security team, plus contract amendments — we can support an auditor access mechanism or a secure log export.
[03:38] [00:04:00] Sofia Martinez: sorry quick interruption — you mentioned key rotation records, are those stored centrally? we need the rotation history for third-party audits.
[03:47] Devon Park: Yes. for our hosted KMS instances we keep key rotation metadata for a rolling period; for Dedicated/VPC you control the KMS and thus the rotation history. we can provide rotation logs as part of the evidence package when the key is managed by Redwood.
[04:05] Maya Chen: On the CAIQ side, we'll mark items as "Evidence provided by Redwood", "Customer to provide", or "Joint". we'll go question-by-question in the template but the faster approach is to identify ownership for the 20 highest-risk clauses.
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: Can you give an example of joint responsibility?
[04:25] Devon Park: Sure. Identity & Access Management: Redwood enforces RBAC inside the console and via tokens; you are responsible for SSO provisioning and enforcing MFA in your IdP. So the CAIQ answer is joint; evidence: Redwood provides RBAC config exports, customer provides SAML metadata and SSO audit logs.
[04:46] Anita Rao: How about encryption in transit — TLS certs and ciphers?
[04:49] Devon Park: We use TLS1.3 and strong ciphers, certs are managed by Redwood for hosted endpoints. for private setups we can accept customer certs or run mutual TLS if required. we will link the cipher suites in the security pack.
[05:02] [00:08:00] Maya Chen: Let's surface the common pain points: customers often struggle with the evidence collection process being manual. we've built a suggested evidence orchestration flow: 1) Redwood pre-populates provider-side answers and attachments; 2) Customer assigns section owners in their org; 3) Joint review call to validate; 4) Redwood uploads provider evidence to secure share; 5) customer archives to their long-term store.
[05:28] Sophia? sorry Sofia?
[05:30] Sofia Martinez: yeah, that flow helps. we want an API or automated sync — manual uploads won't scale for many questionnaires.
[05:36] Devon Park: Totally agree. we have a semi-automated tooling: a secure intake portal where you can push CAIQ and we pre-fill sections and then you can attach additional docs. full API-based sync is on the roadmap; for now we can script S3 syncs and there's a signed URL workflow.
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: Any precedent with auditors wanting original evidence instead of screenshots?
[05:57] Devon Park: Auditors prefer original artifacts — log files, timestamps, cryptographic material where applicable. we try to provide original exports wherever permitted; screenshots are fallback.
[06:08] Anita Rao: On KMS - in our policy we require customer KMS in region eu-west-1 with HSM-backed keys. is that supported?
[06:15] Devon Park: For Dedicated in a VPC, yes — you can bring your own keys in eu-west-1. For hosted, our managed keys may be in consolidated regions; we can talk about region pinning as an enterprise contract term but it's less common for the multi-tenant hosted API.
[06:32] Maya Chen: I'll note that region pinning typically goes with a Dedicated commitment.
[06:36] [00:12:00] Sofia Martinez: Another question — audit log schema: what fields do you export? we need request id, user identity, model id, prompt hash, response token counts, and timestamp.
[06:48] Devon Park: Our raw audit export includes request_id, tenant_id, caller_identity, model_version, input_size, output_size, cost_token_count, timestamp, and a truncated prompt hash by default. we can extend the export to include a full prompt hash or pointer to KV cache references if needed; for privacy reasons we don't export full prompts in hosted unless configured.
[07:14] Anita Rao: That truncated prompt hash might be insufficient for some investigations. Is there a way to keep raw prompts in a private instance?
[07:20] Devon Park: Yes — in private/dedicated deployments you can configure the runtime to log full prompts to your storage endpoint. again that is a contract/config capability and includes additional compliance checks.
[07:35] Maya Chen: let's cover evidence delivery options quickly — secure file share (SFTP), temporary auditor access, signed S3 export, and our secure intake portal. which do you prefer?
[07:46] Liam O'Connor: Prefer S3 signed exports that land in our internal bucket — that fits procurement controls.
[07:51] Devon Park: We'll plan for signed S3 export for the initial evidence set.
[07:55] [00:16:00] Anita Rao: One thing that's been sticky: access controls for Redwood employees during an audit — can you provide a list of employees with elevated access and proof of background checks?
[08:06] Devon Park: We provide role-based access lists and, for auditors, a summary of our background check policy. Individual personnel data is redacted but we can attest that staff with privileged roles have background checks and 2FA enforced.
[08:20] Maya Chen: There was a question earlier on whether Redwood keeps API request bodies for more than 90 days in hosted. I want to be clear: hosted keeps raw request bodies no more than 30 days unless otherwise agreed. aggregated telemetry is longer.
[08:34] Anita Rao: that's shorter than our standard. we'll likely require a Dedicated pilot for regulated PII workloads.
[08:40] Devon Park: Understandable. Dev note: for pilot we'll propose a Dedicated environment with customer-managed storage export and KMS keys, that should meet PII retention and residency requirements.
[08:52] [00:20:00] Sofia Martinez: About the CAIQ, do you have a sample filled CAIQ we can review to speed up mapping?
[08:58] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll attach a sample CAIQ with common provider answers and a few redacted evidence files.
[09:04] Liam O'Connor: okay procurement notes — any legal constraints around auditor access or data exports? need to know for our PO.
[09:11] Maya Chen: Our standard is to allow auditor access under NDA and scoped engagement; data exports are governed by the contract and we can add data transfer addenda for specific residency or retention terms.
[09:24] Anita Rao: For the evidence plan, can you also include your process for incident response artifacts — timelines of notification, post-mortem access?
[09:31] Devon Park: We'll include incident response playbook excerpts and sample post-mortem templates. we can provide a redacted incident timeline as evidence.
[09:40] Maya Chen: quick check — any other blockers on your side that would stop the initial pilot?
[09:45] Anita Rao: Staffing to collect CAIQ pieces is the main blocker. we'll need owners assigned.
[09:50] Liam O'Connor: Budget is TBD but procurement is fine to engage in pilot under limited commitment.
[09:56] [00:24:00] Sofia Martinez: small nit — do you support SSO provisioning SCIM? we prefer automated user provisioning into RBAC groups.
[10:03] Devon Park: Yes. Redwood supports SAML2.0 SSO and SCIM for group provisioning. evidence we can provide: IDP metadata, SCIM logs for provisioning events, and mapping tables for group-to-role.
[10:18] Anita Rao: Good. And for RBAC audits can we get periodic exports of role assignments?
[10:22] Devon Park: Yes — role assignment exports are available via API or CSV dump. we'll include a sample in the pack.
[10:29] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline: we'll send the cert/evidence pack by Thursday (that's 2026-07-30), you assign SIG owners, and then we do a joint review next week. sound right?
[10:40] Anita Rao: sounds good.
[10:42] Liam O'Connor: yes.
[10:44] [00:28:00] Maya Chen: A couple of tricky CAIQ questions often trip customers — supply chain security, third-party sub processors, and data deletion proofs. For sub processors we maintain a list and contract flowdowns; for deletion proofs we can provide deletion job logs for customer-owned buckets.
[11:03] Anita Rao: Will you give us the subprocessor list as part of the pack?
[11:06] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll include our subprocessors and their locations.
[11:10] Sofia Martinez: One last technical: model determinism and model hashing — auditors sometimes ask about model immutability and versioning. how do you show model lineage?
[11:19] Devon Park: Our serving runtime logs model_version and model artifact checksum on each deployment. we can export deployment manifests showing versions and checksums for the timeframe in question.
[11:33] Maya Chen: Okay, we're approaching 45 minutes. final recap?
[11:37] Anita Rao: Please send pack with SOC 2 summary, CAIQ sample, subprocessors, and a plan for the Dedicated pilot including KMS in eu-west-1.
[11:47] Maya Chen: We'll do that. Devon, capture the technical deliverables?
[11:50] Devon Park: Captured — I'll prepare the evidence upload instructions, sample role exports, and the audit log export spec.
[11:56] Maya Chen: Great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the links and set the joint review on the calendar.
[11:59] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
[12:01] Meeting end.
